correction.text: without Esztergom, Nové Zámky and Buda

keyframe_review.note: Buda 'fell on 2 September' 1686 after 78 days; 'Turkish resistance then collapsed across the region'.

1687-1698: the page gives no town after Buda except Belgrade (1688, retaken 1690) and Slankamen (1691, Habsburg possession of Hungary and Transylvania secured). Bridging reading: only the Temeşvar eyalet (the Banat), which the Ottoman Hungary page has the Ottomans cede only at Passarowitz in 1718; low confidence, and Nagyvárad's fate between 1664 and 1699 is not on a page opened.

ledger.note: 1541: the Ottomans take Buda and form Budin Eyalet. 'In 1541, Suleyman decided to consolidate the conquered Buda area and to set it up as an organic part of the Empire'; 'He immediately organised the first Central European eyalet (province) with its capital in Buda (Budin in Turkish)'; infobox 'Founded: 29 August 1541'.

region.text: Nógrád, Vác, Fehérvár, Pécs and Siklós

ledger.note: 1543-44: the Ottomans take more fortresses. 'took Nógrád, Vác, Fehérvár, Pécs, and Siklós in 1543-44' and added them to the eyalet (page paraphrase; the page gives 1543-44, the year 1543 is the first). The Long Turkish War page says Vác had been held 'since 1541': the pages differ.

region.text: the northern sanjaks of the c.1566 list (reading)

ledger.note: 1552: northern expansion. 'In 1552 the eyalet was expanded with new territories in the North'; the page names no town, so the region is the northern sanjaks of its c.1566 list (Hatvan, Szécsény, Szolnok and others). The counterpart is my reading: the Esztergom and Veszprém sanjaks of the list are the part held by royal Hungary's side; the page names no former holder.
1552: the Eyalet of Temeşvar is established ('the new Eyalet of Temeşvar was established'); the Ottoman Hungary page lists it among the six eyalets. The page does not say who held the Banat.

region.text: the frontier fortresses of Veszprém, Győr, Komárom, Esztergom, Székesfehérvár and Eger

ledger.note: 1593: the Long Turkish War opens on Hungarian soil. 'The Long Turkish War started on July 29, 1593'; the first ground fought over is the sieges of Veszprém and Várpalota in October 1593.
1594: the Ottomans take the two Danube fortresses. 'Ottomans captured Győr and Komárom' in 1594.

region.text: Esztergom and Visegrád on the Danube

ledger.note: 1595: 'Mansfeld's Christian forces captured Esztergom and Visegrád on the Danube'.

1596: the Ottomans take Eger and form the Eğri eyalet. The Budin page has 'the establishment of the eyalets of Eğri (1596)'; the Long Turkish War page has 'Ottomans conquered Eger' and the Battle of Mezőkeresztes on 24-26 October 1596.
1598: 'Habsburg forces retook Győr and Komárom'.

1600: the Kanije (Nagykanizsa) eyalet is established ('Kanije (1600)'). The Long Turkish War page dates only the failed Habsburg siege of Nagykanizsa to 1601 and says the Ottomans 'kept Eger and Kanizsa' in 1606; the capture itself is not dated on a page opened.
11 November 1606: the Peace of Zsitvatorok. The Habsburgs 'Received Vác, which the Ottomans had held since 1541'; the Ottomans 'Kept Eger and Kanizsa'.

region.text: the frontier fortresses of Veszprém, Győr, Komárom, Esztergom, Székesfehérvár and Eger

ledger.note: 11 November 1606: Zsitvatorok ends the Long Turkish War; 'The war was indecisive, with little territory changing hands'.

27 August 1660: Nagyvárad (Oradea) falls to the Ottomans: 'The fall of Nagyvárad to the expansionist Ottomans on 27 August 1660 marked the decline of the Principality' (Transylvania page). The Peace of Vasvár (10 August 1664) then recognised 'Ottoman control of Transylvania, Nagyvarad (Grosswardein) and Ersekujvar' (Austro-Turkish War page). [Reviewer eu-15-x: moved from 1664 with counterpart habsburg-monarchy; Várad was Transylvanian, and principality-of-transylvania books the 1660-08 loss.]
1663: the Austro-Turkish War ('12 April 1663 - 10 August 1664') reaches Slovakia: the Ottoman army 'in September conquered the town of' Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky).
September 1663: Nové Zámky falls to the Ottomans and becomes the Uyvar frontier eyalet (the Ottoman Hungary infobox lists Uyvar).
10 August 1664: 'the Peace of Vasvár was signed'; the Habsburgs recognise Ottoman control of 'Transylvania, Nagyvárad, and Érsekújvár'.

region.text: Ottoman Hungary, the front of the Great Turkish War

ledger.note: 1683: the Great Turkish War: the main Ottoman army 'laid siege to Vienna on 14 July 1683'; the first ground lost in Hungary is Esztergom, which surrendered 'after a short siege' following the victory at Párkány in October 1683.
October 1683: 'Victory at Párkány in October 1683 led to Esztergom surrendering after a short siege.'
19 August 1685: 'Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky) fell on 19 August'.

2 September 1686: Buda falls. 'After 78 days of siege, the city fell on 2 September'; Buda had been Ottoman since 1541. Budin page: 'On 2 September 1686 Budin was captured by the troops of the Holy League.'

1687: bridging. After Buda 'Turkish resistance then collapsed across the region' and the second Battle of Mohács was 'a crushing defeat for the Sultan' (page, no year-by-year towns); the region lost is my reading: everything but the Temeşvar eyalet (the Banat), which the Passarowitz sentence of the Ottoman Hungary page keeps Ottoman to 1718. Page silent on towns.

region.text: Ottoman Hungary, the front of the Great Turkish War

ledger.note: January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz ends the Great Turkish War ('26 January 1699' in the infobox, '22 January 1699' in the body of the page).

January 1699: 'the Ottomans recognized the loss of the Ottoman Hungary by the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699'; 'The Ottomans ceded most of Hungary, Transylvania and Slavonia' (Great Turkish War page). The Temeşvar eyalet stayed Ottoman until the cession acknowledged at Passarowitz in 1718, so the last land of the dossier returns to the Ottoman Empire's own row.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of central Hungary
wars.outcome: The Ottomans form Budin Eyalet in 1541, add Nógrád, Vác, Fehérvár, Pécs and Siklós in 1543-44 and create the Temeşvar eyalet in 1552.
wars.note: Named by me from the Budin page's account; no Wikipedia article was opened under this title.

wars.name: Long Turkish War
wars.outcome: Indecisive: the Ottomans kept Eger and Kanizsa, the Habsburgs got Vác; peace of Zsitvatorok on 11 November 1606.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663-1664)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Nové Zámky in September 1663 and kept it, with Nagyvárad, at the Peace of Vasvár on 10 August 1664.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Holy League takes Esztergom (1683), Nové Zámky (1685), Buda (2 September 1686) and wins at Mohács (1687), Slankamen (1691) and Zenta (11 September 1697); Karlowitz in January 1699 cedes most of Hungary.

certainty.note: The frontier was a line of fortresses ('heavily fortified with troop garrisons'), not a survey line; the treaties of 1606 and 1664 name fortresses, not boundaries. The Karlowitz frontier of 1699 is the first treaty line, but the page opened gives no boundary description.

notes:
Ottoman Hungary is a state Cliopatria lacks: Cliopatria draws the occupied centre as the Kingdom of Hungary to 1546 and then inside the Ottoman Empire row. Typed colony (Ottoman province drawn as a vassal tint of ottoman-empire); the ottoman-empire dossier books the same land as direct Ottoman gains (1541, 1663, 1686, 1699), so the colour agent must pick one. Page budget 5; pages used: five.

Not settled: (1) the founding of Varat (Nagyvárad) and Uyvar eyalets: the Ottoman Hungary infobox lists both, no page opened dates the founding (Uyvar follows the September 1663 capture; Oradea is Ottoman by the 1664 treaty). (2) The towns lost between 1687 and 1698: the Great Turkish War page names none; the 1687 loss is a bridging reading at confidence 1, and the fate of Nagyvárad (Ottoman by the 1664 treaty) between 1664 and 1699 is on no page opened. (3) The Sanjak lists of the Budin page include Serbian, Slavonian and Banat sanjaks (Semendire, Pojega, Sirem, Çanad), which the 'Ottoman Hungary' article does not count; only the Hungarian part and the Banat are drawn here. (4) Vác: the Budin page says taken in 1543-44, the Long Turkish War page says held 'since 1541'. (5) The Karlowitz date: 26 January 1699 in the infobox, 22 January in the body of the Great Turkish War page. (6) Esztergom was Ottoman again by 1683 after the Habsburg capture of 1595; the date of the Ottoman recapture is on no page opened (see royal-hungary).

Gazetteer: no gaps; places given by coordinates (Vác, Siklós, Komárom, Visegrád, Eger, Nové Zámky) for lack of gazetteer entries.
